title: Verve Signs Maggie Kuntz (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Verve has signed film, television and theater actress Maggie Kuntz for representation, Variety has learned exclusively. She continues to be repped b
body:
Verve has signed film, television and theater actress Maggie Kuntz for representation, Variety has learned exclusively. She continues to be repped by The Rosenzweig Group. 

	Kuntz recently joined the cast of the Focus Features film “The Bell Jar,” based on the iconic Sylvia Plath novel of the same name. The cast also includes Billie Eilish, Carey Mulligan, Connor Storrie, and Danielle Deadwyler. Kuntz will play Esther Greenwood’s (Eilish) best friend and confidante Doreen. 
	

	Kuntz is also set to appear in the fourth season of the hit HBO series “The Gilded Age.” She will play Fiona Summers, a cousin of the Astor family and a new arrival in New York high society. 


	On stage, Kuntz recently starred in the Broadway production of “John Proctor Is the Villain,” while she has also been a part of the Broadway show based on “The Outsiders.”

title: Graham Norton Shoots Down ‘Conspiracy Theory’ That Taylor Swift’s ‘Opalite’ Video Was Shot Before She Came on His Show
description:
Graham Norton has shot down a “conspiracy theory” surrounding Taylor Swift’s “Opalite” music video, in which he guest stars.

	Speaking at the Royal
body:
Graham Norton has shot down a “conspiracy theory” surrounding Taylor Swift’s “Opalite” music video, in which he guest stars.

	Speaking at the Royal Television Society conference in London, Norton said seeing his famous “The Graham Norton Show” sofa brought to life in Swift’s video was “really odd” and “made my dreams come true.”

	But he debunked a rumor circulating online that Swift first filmed the music video – which stars Domhnall Gleeson, Greta Lee, Jodie Turner-Smith, Cillian Murphy and Lewis Capaldi — and then arranged for its cast to appear on Norton’s show.
	

	“The Swifties, they love a conspiracy theory,” he said, referring to Swift’s army of fans. “So there were Swifties who thought we’d filmed the music video first and then orchestrated to get all the people on the sofa.”


	Broadcaster Tina Daheley, who was interviewing Norton on stage, interjected: “It was literally an idea she came up with while she was on the show.”

	Norton replied: “Yeah, yeah. I don’t know, but certainly when you watch the clips, there is a moment when it looks like she’s having the idea, and it’s kind of amazing to have the show get that kind of recognition.”

	The video, which was released in February this year, features Swift and Gleeson as two unlucky in love singles who eventually find their way to one another, taking part in a dance contest on the way. Lee, Turner-Smith, Murphy and Capaldi all make cameo appearances.

	Swift appeared on Norton’s BBC show – which famously has an eclectic mix of celebrity guests each week — last October, appearing alongside Gleeson, Lee, Turner-Smith, Murphy and Capaldi. 
	

	During the recording, Gleeson quipped about appearing in one of Swift’s music videos at which point, she later revealed, the concept “crash-landed into my imagination” while still sat on Norton’s sofa.

schema.headline: Graham Norton Shoots Down ‘Conspiracy Theory’ That Taylor Swift’s ‘Opalite’ Video Was Shot Before She Came on His Show

title: Disney Makes More Job Cuts, Laying Off a Few Hundred Employees
description:
Disney continues to cut heads: The media company is laying off a few hundred employees across multiple departments, Variety has confirmed.

	The lay
body:
Disney continues to cut heads: The media company is laying off a few hundred employees across multiple departments, Variety has confirmed.

	The layoffs, the third round this year under recently appointed CEO Josh D’Amaro, are primarily in Disney’s human resources and IT departments across corporate and within different divisions, according to a source familiar with the cuts.

	In announcing results for the June 2026 quarter, D’Amaro and CFO Hugh Johnston indicated that more job cutbacks were coming. “We remain highly focused on reducing costs across the enterprise to create incremental capacity to invest for growth and are evaluating a variety of levers, including reductions in labor and SG&A,” the latter referring to selling, general and administrative expenses, the execs wrote in the Aug. 5 letter to Disney shareholders. “We are mid-stream in this work and will provide future updates on our progress.”
	

	The latest waves of layoffs come after Disney in April eliminated about 1,000 roles, primarily as a result of D’Amaro’s formation of a consolidated enterprise marketing division under the leadership of Asad Ayaz, chief marketing and brand officer. In July, it made further job cuts, Disney eliminating several hundred jobs across certain corporate functions, including at Pixar, ESPN, Disney Entertainment Television and Disney’s studios. The majority of the layoffs on the studios side were within Pixar and majority of cuts in the TV group were at National Geographic.

	In August, Disney offered early-retirement buyout packages to longtime executives, as part of its ongoing cost-cutting efforts.
	

	Disney reported having about 231,000 full- and part-time employees as of September 2025 (the end of its fiscal year). The layoffs Tuesday were first reported by Deadline.

schema.headline: Disney Makes More Job Cuts, Laying Off a Few Hundred Employees

title: Cinema United Sets New Executive Promotions
description: Trade association Cinema United has appointed Amanda Martin to the newly created role of senior vice president of external affairs, also promoting E
body:
Trade association Cinema United has appointed Amanda Martin to the newly created role of senior vice president of external affairs, also promoting Erin Von Hoetzendorff to vice president of membership and global affairs.

	“As exhibition continues to evolve, Cinema United is evolving with it,” said Michael O’Leary, the president and CEO of Cinema United. “These two well-deserved promotions will allow us to strengthen our partnerships across the entertainment ecosystem, deepen our advocacy on behalf of all theatre owners and expand our engagement with international theater owners, ensuring that every constituency we serve has a strong voice within our organization. Amanda and Erin are critical to our success, and in these new roles, they will have even greater impact on the direction and future of Cinema United.”
	

	Both appointments begin immediately and are aimed to reflect Cinema United’s incentive to meet the needs of exhibition today and in the near future. The organization serves as the largest exhibition trade organization in the world, representing more than 60,000 movie screens globally.


	“Together, these roles will help Cinema United serve exhibition more completely and effectively than ever before,” O’Leary added. “One strengthens our connections across the industry itself and elevates our advocacy on behalf of our members; the other strengthens our connection to theater owners around the world. Both are essential to how we grow and represent our members going forward.”

	Martin previously held the role of chief of staff for three years and will continue to serve as a senior member of Cinema United’s leadership team. In her new role, she will strengthen the organization’s relationships, lead educational programming for industry events and oversee its state government affairs function. Martin will also continue to serve as a federal advocate before Congress and federal agencies alongside O’Leary.
	

	Von Hoetzendorff joined Cinema United in 2018, previously serving as the head of membership services. She will now lead the organization’s engagement with international theater owners, building on Cinema United’s mission to provide representation and support for exhibitors across the world.

schema.headline: Cinema United Sets New Executive Promotions

title: Variety and Outfront Announce Experience and Culture Summit: The IRL Advantage, Featuring Questlove, Charlamagne tha God and Ice-T
description:
Sep 29, 2026 10:00am PT	
	

	
		Variety and Outfront Announce Experience and Culture Summit: The IRL Advantage, Featuring Questlove,
body:
Sep 29, 2026 10:00am PT	
	

	
		Variety and Outfront Announce Experience and Culture Summit: The IRL Advantage, Featuring Questlove, Charlamagne tha God and Ice-T
	

	The invite-only Oct. 7 summit in New York brings together marketing leaders from Ulta Beauty, Snap, American Express, NBCUniversal, the NFL, MLS and the WTA to explore why real-world experience is moving to the center of marketing
	
			


			
			
	

									Christian Germoso
	

		
	
				
	Variety and Outfront today announced the first-ever Variety Experience and Culture Summit: The IRL Advantage presented by Outfront, taking place Oct. 7 in New York at The Penn District by Skylight. The invite-only event will bring together artists, brand CMOs, sports leaders and media executives for candid conversations on how live, real-world experiences build fandom, fuel creativity and move audiences to act, with appearances by Questlove, Charlamagne tha God and Ice-T.
	

	As attention fragments across endless feeds and screens, the moments people choose to show up for in person have become some of the most valuable in media. Brands, sports organizations and entertainment companies are looking beyond the screen to reach audiences where they gather — at games, concerts, festivals and premieres, and on the streets of the cities they live in. The summit will explore what that shift means for marketers and how to put it to work.


	“Partnering with Outfront on this first-ever summit reflects exactly the conversation the industry needs to be having right now,” said Michelle Fine-Smith, SVP, Global B2B Partnerships, Variety. “The leaders joining us, from CMOs rethinking brand experience to entertainers and sports icons building lifelong fandom, will explore why the IRL advantage, real-world connection, has become something that can’t be automated. There’s no better place to have that conversation than New York, a city that just celebrated a historic Knicks championship.”

	“There’s a lot of talk about what in real-life (IRL) media means, but there’s no one-size-fits-all formula for breaking through to the audiences that matter most,” said Julie Massoni, Head of Enterprise Sales, West Coast, Outfront. “For an entertainment industry changing this quickly, IRL media is how you meet that disruption head-on — whether you’re driving attention to a series, a theatrical release, a concert, a festival or a sporting event, or you’re a brand trying to reach fans through them. This summit is about real examples of real-world campaigns that delivered real results.”
	

	Programming highlights include:


Questlove, Grammy-winning musician, Academy Award-winning filmmaker and New York Times best-selling author, on how the energy of a live audience shapes his work with The Roots, from their role as house band for “The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon” to the group’s expansion in an annual festival with the acclaimed Roots Picnic.
Charlamagne tha God, multimedia mogul and co-host of The Breakfast Club, will discuss his approach to building unique experiences for his passionate fan base, including the Black Effect Podcast Festival, and how live experiences fuel his creativity across platforms, including top-rated radio program “The Breakfast Club.”
Ice-T, who stars in “Law & Order: SVU” as Sgt. Odafin “Fin” Tutuola; Mark Marshall, Chairman, Global Advertising and Partnerships, NBCUniversal; Rachael Zaluzec, Chief Marketing Officer and SVP, Customer Experience, Volkswagen of America; and Julie Scelzo, Chief Creative Officer of Xfinity, Comcast will discuss how NBCUniversal drives fandom across must-see experiences, live studio audiences and more, as well as explore how brands can authentically participate in these cultural driving moments. The conversation – marking NBC’s 100th anniversary – will be moderated by Savannah Sellers, Anchor, NBC News NOW; NBC News Correspondent.
Outfront CEO Nick Brien in a keynote conversation on why experience is becoming central to the next generation of marketing.
Rafael Espinal, Commissioner of the New York City Mayor’s Office of Media and Entertainment, on how New York continues to serve as a massive IRL stage and a catalyst for community, culture and large-scale experiences.
Ulta Beauty CMO Kelly Mahoney, Dick’s Sporting Goods CMO Emily Silver, Snap CMO Grace Kao, Land O’Lakes CMO Heather Malenshek and Instacart Head of Commercial Marketing Stephanie Paturzo-Swingle on the experience economy: why brands are making real-world engagement a core part of their consumer strategies, and how innovation is reshaping the events landscape.
“IRL Advantage: Building Trust in an Agentic World,” a panel with Kantar CEO, Americas Jeff Greenspoon, Snap Head of Research, Consumer Insights and Strategy Aarti Bhaskaran and Outfront Chief Marketing and Experience Officer Stacy Minero, will dive into what data reveals about the positive business impact of real-world audience interaction.
NFL CMO Tim Ellis, Major League Soccer CMO Radhika Duggal, New York Giants SVP, Marketing and Brand Strategy Nilay Shah and Women’s Tennis Association Chief Brand Officer Sarah Swanson on what it takes to turn fans into lifelong followers, and how brands can tap into the cultural power of sports.
A look at the future of experiential entertainment, including emerging technologies, AI and new approaches to event design, with Paul Caine, President, On Location, TKO Group Holdings (UFC, WWE); Christine Cassis, CMO, Twitch; Bess Spaeth, EVP, Global Brand Management & Experiences, American Express; Josephine Vaccarello, EVP, Live, Madison Square Garden; and Benoit Vatere, Chief Media and Digital Commerce Officer, Liquid Death.



	The Variety Experience and Culture Summit: The IRL Advantage presented by Outfront is invite-only. To request an invitation, visit variety.com/outfrontexperience.


	
		More from Variety

title: Prime Video, Sony, JioStar, Zee and NDTV Chiefs on How Connected TV Is Reshaping Indian Storytelling
description: Connected TV is changing what Indian media companies make, not just where audiences watch it, with Prime Video now developing shows around whether a
body:
Connected TV is changing what Indian media companies make, not just where audiences watch it, with Prime Video now developing shows around whether audiences will watch them together, executives said at the FICCI-Frames conference in Mumbai.

	Streaming began as a largely solo experience, Gaurav Gandhi, VP and head of Prime Video for Asia-Pacific and Australia-New Zealand, said during the opening presentation, “India’s Screen Economy – The Next Wave.” “So much of our time is being spent today thinking about like, hey, this is a co-viewing show compared to this is an individual-driven show first,” he said.
	

	Gandhi said CTV combines the shared, lean-back experience of television with digital’s convenience, choice and ad targeting. “The challenge it brings up with is in that world of so much choice, when you’re in a lean-back experience, how easy do you make it for customers to be able to get to what you want to get to?” he said, adding that recommendation engines need to get much better.


	Moderator Vivek Couto, co-founder, CEO and executive director of Media Partners Asia, described CTV as a screen that pairs TV’s scale with digital’s addressability and asked the panel how it would reshape the industry’s economics.

	Kevin Vaz, chair of the FICCI Media & Entertainment Committee and CEO of entertainment at JioStar, said he would rather talk about the large screen than about CTV specifically. “The large screen has always been communion, the large screen has always brought families together and been a unifier,” he said. CTV keeps that and adds measurement and addressability, Vaz said, letting advertisers, most of whom prefer the bigger screen, aim their messages at specific audiences. Citing the figure presented earlier in the session, he put India’s CTV audience at nearly 200 million viewers and said it is growing fast.
	

	Gaurav Banerjee, managing director and CEO of Sony Pictures Networks India, recalled the old marketing line “Medium is the message” and said industry discourse can get swayed by the signal rather than the substance. “So it finally doesn’t really matter how people get to that large-screen experience, but what do they do when they get there?” he said.

	For Banerjee, CTV offers the same opportunity TV has offered for three decades: a family gathered around a program it can talk about over dinner. The industry’s job is to create those viewing experiences, he said, recalling watching “Nukkad” with his family as a child in the 1980s. “I think that’s something that hasn’t truly changed and should not change, and that’s something that we have to keep building and keep protecting,” he said.

	For news, CTV is opening up programming that linear schedules could not justify. Rahul Kanwal, CEO and editor-in-chief of NDTV, said linear planners always worry that a show with narrow appeal will sink a channel’s ratings. On CTV, NDTV has been able to double down on “Lifeline,” about healthcare, wellness and anti-aging, and “Launchpad,” about upskilling. “News channels typically wouldn’t be able to do that kind of content because there wouldn’t be enough eyeballs in that,” Kanwal said, adding that CTV viewers open such content only if they are interested.

	Vaz said the definition of a hit has shifted as screens have multiplied. Success used to be judged on a single large-screen measure, he said, but now also counts audience votes, engagement and social media trends. Technology, he added, can match each story with the viewer it suits, when and where they want it, so that one person’s flop can be another’s hit.

	Punit Goenka, CEO of Zee Entertainment Enterprises, said the industry has moved beyond the TV-versus-digital split into an attention economy, where content, technology and data have to work together. Asked what makes content win amid endless choice, he kept it to a single line. “Infinite content does not mean infinite consumption,” he said.

schema.headline: Prime Video, Sony, JioStar, Zee and NDTV Chiefs on How Connected TV Is Reshaping Indian Storytelling

title: ITV Boss, Sky’s Content Chief Set Out Vision for Acquisition, Try to Calm Nerves: ‘The Competition is Ferocious’
description: With Comcast-owned Sky’s $2.1 billion acquisition of ITV currently winding its way through the regulatory process in the U.K., both parties are limi
body:
With Comcast-owned Sky’s $2.1 billion acquisition of ITV currently winding its way through the regulatory process in the U.K., both parties are limited in how much they can say. Yet Sky’s content chief Cecile Frot-Coutaz and ITV CEO Carolyn McCall, both speaking in separate keynote speeches at the Royal Television Society convention in London, managed to say quite a lot about what the deal means for the U.K.

	Read on for their comments on key aspects of the deal including content and news…
	
	
		How the deal happened…	

	Frot-Cotaz and McCall both acknowledged the television landscape has shifted immeasurably over the past decade. McCall said the Sky/ITV acquisition “wouldn’t have gone through” even six years ago, with the Competition and Markets Authority taking a much more bullish approach to consolidation in the past.

	“The transaction is very much a response to what’s happened in the marketplace,” Frot-Cotaz said. But she added, Sky are not just acquiring ITV to create a “robust” media company: “we think there’s a lot of opportunity in it as well.”

	Five years ago there was 200,000 hours of streaming content available to audiences – that has now more than doubled to 900,000, a figure that doesn’t include YouTube, said the ITV boss. “That’s what we’re up against.”
	
		Content is still king…	

	Both Frot-Coutaz and McCall said Sky was committed to ITV content, not least because the deal terms include a content supply agreement with ITV Studios.

	“One of the most important things to Sky was our content,” McCall said in an attempt to allay fears amongst indie produces that cost savings will result in less money going into content. “There’ll be more content because the sum of the two.”
	

	In her keynote Frot-Coutaz agreed: “The goal ultimately is to maintain the scale of the content offering.”
	
		Investment in tech…	

	“The competition is ferocious,” McCall said. “It’s not just [being] bigger; it’s also the investment. So you have to invest in technology. You’ve got to continue to invest in AI. You’ve got to continue to invest in efficiency, and most importantly, you’ve got to have to enough money to constantly invest in content, because content is where it’s at. That’s what makes you all your money.”

	Frot-Coutaz echoed that. “Content is super important, but you also need the technology that goes with it.”

	But technology costs money and for money you need scale. Hence the deal.
	
		Commitment to news…	

	A key concern around the acquisition is whether Sky will seek to consolidate its newsroom with ITV’s. While ITV’s public service broadcasting commitments — which includes nations, regional and national news — are protected until 2034, there is a large question mark over what will happen after that day.

	McCall said that ITN, which makes ITV’s news (it operates under a shared-ownership scheme comprised of four stakeholders, one of which is ITV) is a “strong news organization” so asked “why would you duplicate?”

	Frot-Coutaz maintained that Sky has made a “very public commitment to maintain Sky News and to maintain ITN news” but refused to say whether that commitment would extend past 2034, when ITV’s public service broadcast license expires.

	Whether that will allay fears remains to be seen. Watch this space.

schema.headline: ITV Boss, Sky’s Content Chief Set Out Vision for Acquisition, Try to Calm Nerves: ‘The Competition is Ferocious’

title: ‘Love Hypothesis’ Sequel in the Works at Amazon MGM and MRC, Based on Author Ali Hazelwood’s New Book ‘The Two-Body Problem’
description: Author Ali Hazelwood took to Instagram on Tuesday morning to reveal that “The Two-Body Problem,” a sequel to her 2021 novel “The Love Hypothesis,” h
body:
Author Ali Hazelwood took to Instagram on Tuesday morning to reveal that “The Two-Body Problem,” a sequel to her 2021 novel “The Love Hypothesis,” hits shelves in February 2027. She also revealed that MRC is developing a film based on a new book for Amazon MGM Studios.

	“‘I wrote a sequel to The Love Hypothesis‘ is not a sentence I thought I’d say a year or so ago, but now I weirdly can’t imagine a world in which ‘The Two-Body Problem’ doesn’t exist,” Hazelwood wrote, sharing the cover of “The Love Hypothesis.” “I’m really eager to talk more about this book and how it came about in the next few months. For now let me just say that the ‘TLH’ movie and its cast made me fall for Adam and Olive all over again, that revisiting them was an absolute pleasure.“
	

	She added, “As someone who gets VERY attached to stories and characters, I know that unannounced sequels can be blindsiding, so feel free to skip this book and overwrite it with whatever headcanon you prefer, and I’ll see you on the next one!”


	Hazelwood then dropped the news about the film. While prefacing that “nothing is guaranteed,” she confirmed that “MRC is developing” a “Two-Body Problem” movie for Amazon MGM.


	The first book in the series, “The Love Hypothesis,” was a New York Times bestseller and a BookTok sensation. The rom-com was recently adapted into a movie for Prime Video, hitting the platform on Sept. 23. Lili Reinhart and Tom Bateman starred. Claire Scanlon directed, with a script by Sarah Rothschild.
	

	“The Love Hypothesis” follows brainy graduate student Olive Smith, who starts a fake relationship with Adam Carlsen, a fellow scientist and a notoriously harsh professor known as “Dr. Evil” around campus.

schema.headline: ‘Love Hypothesis’ Sequel in the Works at Amazon MGM and MRC, Based on Author Ali Hazelwood’s New Book ‘The Two-Body Problem’

title: Beyond Fest Organizers on Improved Ticketing, Fans ‘As Unhinged as We Are’ and Their 7 Titles Not to Miss
description: How true is the perception that Los Angeles doesn’t have a prominent signature film festival? While the city’s film lovers were debating the questio
body:
How true is the perception that Los Angeles doesn’t have a prominent signature film festival? While the city’s film lovers were debating the question, Beyond Fest at American Cinematheque snuck in and became one of the city’s biggest and most popular cinema events, with some 37,000 people expected by the end of the movie celebration that runs through Oct. 5.

	L.A. has sometimes been a tricky town for film festivals. Over the years, several high-profile fests struggled to stay afloat with consistently strong slates, and dozens of niche festivals filled in the gaps to serve the city’s diverse filmgoers. Then 14 years ago, Beyond Fest stepped in, and by partnering with the American Cinematheque, it was able to build up a fan base so rabid that scoring tickets became a blood sport for the city’s cinephiles.
	

	Despite its October berth and a slate that includes titles like the “Carrie” TV series and the original “Friday the 13th,” the aim has always been to go “beyond” obvious genre classics by programming a wide array of films with varied genre influences.


	This year’s selection includes buzzy new releases like “Primetime” and “Musk” as well as retrospectives from “Hoffa” to “Pan’s Labyrinth,” plus under-the-radar titles that screen for free at the Los Feliz 3 cinemas, thanks to Mubi’s sponsorship.

	“The inspiration was always to be more than strictly horror, back in those early years,” says co-founder Christian Parkes. “(But we also) did ‘Dog Day Afternoon.’ Our film collections and our film tastes and our DVD closets are wildly varied.”
	

	The festival’s explosive growth trajectory coincides with young L.A. audiences’ year-round passion for attending repertory and classic film screenings since the pandemic, with Letterboxd playing a big part in stoking the interest.

	“The rep scene has never been better from an attendance standpoint,” says Parkes, mentioning last week’s Robert Eggers marathon. “It’s a rite of passage now to see these films. It’s not enough to see ‘The Witch’ in a theater now; I have to see ‘The Witch’ with Robert Eggers in person, along with ‘Lighthouse’ and ‘Northman’ and ‘Nosferatu’ and to be able to say, ‘Yeah, I was there.’”

	“Things like Beyond Fest are a signal that things are completely changing,” says Juan Devis, president of Film Independent, the L.A.-based filmmaker organization that runs the Spirit Awards. “Young people are going back to cinema. They’re doing it because they love to do it and they do it constantly.”



	

					Beyond Fest at American Cinematheque co-founder Christian Parkes, left and head of programming Evrim Ersoy
	



	With the film business scrambling to find the next Curry Barker or Kane Parsons, head of programming Evrim Ersoy says the industry is keeping an eye on the shorts blocks that play at the Los Feliz Theater.

	“Studios and agencies come through to those blocks and discover filmmakers and pick them up for the next step in their career,” says Ersoy. 

	Scoring impossible-to-get Beyond Fest tickets is a rite of passage for the city’s young cinephiles, some of whom think nothing of driving an hour from Silver Lake to Santa Monica or vice versa for an in-demand screening.

	“Over the last 14 years, (the festival) has built a core dedicated group who are as unhinged as we are. They will travel from one side of town to the other — they will go from the Aero in Santa Monica and then be in Los Feliz. I love those people because it speaks to how much they love cinema,” says Ersoy.

	Thanks to Beyond’s relationship with the American Cinematheque (the Cinematheque’s artistic director Grant Moninger is the festival’s co-founder), the event doesn’t have to scramble each year to secure new theaters. Screenings are held at all the Cinematheque’s venues — the Aero, the newly reopened Egyptian in Hollywood, the Los Feliz 3 and the Directors Village in Westwood Village.
	

	“We’ve kind of grown in parallel (with the Cinematheque),” says Parkes. “We were rough and ragged and loose around the edges at the same time that the Egyptian Theater was — the carpet was peeling, the floors were a little sticky, but that thing was fun. They’ve matured into this next iteration under Grant Moninger, who’s the artistic and creative director there. It’s great the way that institution has grown and shifted into something bigger,” says Parkes.

	Much to the relief of frequent festgoers, the Cinematheque updated its ticketing system this year, making the scramble for seats a little more efficient, though tickets are still challenging to come by.



	

					“Primetime”
									Courtesy Everett Collection
	



	“It’s impossible to get tickets for Cannes. It’s impossible to get tickets for New York Film Festival. It’s impossible to get tickets for Sundance,” Parkes points out. “There are always people that are going to miss out. The demand to see ‘Your Mother, Your Mother, Your Mother’ and ‘Primetime’ in Los Angeles greatly exceeded the space that we have for these two films to play, so credit to the Cinematheque for completely revamping and creating the completely new ticketing system. You want to see films in a packed theater, and you want to see films with an audience that is excited to be there.”

	This kind of enthusiasm and scarcity is all down to the audience members, who drive the programming rather than the other way around, says Parkes, “It’s the audience that is really defining it and telling us what they want to see.” And it’s all done without spending money on advertising and promotion.

	“The intention was just to create a space where like-minded people that didn’t know each other could come together and find their people. Evrim, myself, and the folks at the American Cinematheque are just kind of custodians,” says Parkes.

	Retrospectives continue to be a big part of the program, often with the filmmakers participating. “There’s so much of an emphasis on new films, new films, new films, but these new films don’t exist without the old films,” says Parkes. “We have M. Night Shyamalan coming to L.A. for the first time in a very long time, and the first time he’s done a retrospective in Los Angeles. That’s super exciting, not just for us but for audiences. It sold out in an instant.” 
	

	Film Independent’s Devis thinks the enthusiastic response is part of a cultural shift. “Young people are looking for something that is authentic, that’s communal, that speaks to them, in a way that the last 10 years of film has not. This constant sort of franchises and IPs — that culture that is completely being dethroned right now, in my opinion.”

	Beyond Fest’s Parkes and Ersoy break down some of their top titles still to screen:

	“Rumble in the Bronx” — “Bob Odenkirk is coming to introduce ‘Rumble in the Bronx’ because he’s a massive Jackie Chan fan,” says Ersoy. “To be in that room, to hear him talk about it to an audience who hasn’t seen the film — It’s a great way to contextualize, and they have a way in, and they connect with the film in a really intense way.”

	“Donnie Darko” — “We’ve got ‘Donnie Darko’ showing at the Aero Theater where it was shot, and that’s really exciting.”

	“Miami Vice” — “We’ve got this new cut of ‘Miami Vice,’ which has had a bit of a renaissance recently.”

	“Welcome to G-Town” — “Two brothers from Glasgow made a film for less than $10,000 straight out of school, and they’re here, and it’s like early Peter Jackson, very Scottish humor.”

	“Ten Will” — “There’s an L.A. filmmaker, Max DeFalco. $75,000 budget, shot in L.A. He’s awesome, a massive future talent.”

	“Wicker” — “The BookTok people out there are ravenous.”

	“Ken Russell’s The Devils” — “The one that I am most excited for, we screened it about 10 years ago,” says Parkes. “Being able to have this moment and bring this thing full circle with two simultaneous screenings in the Egyptian Theatre and in the Aero Theatre, both on 35mm, the West Coast premiere of the 4k restoration director’s cut. That’s going to be one for the ages, and that is a quintessential Beyond Fest film and a quintessential Beyond Fest moment.”

schema.headline: Beyond Fest Organizers on Improved Ticketing, Fans ‘As Unhinged as We Are’ and Their 7 Titles Not to Miss

title: Berlanti Productions Promotes Liam Driscoll to Creative Executive (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Berlanti Productions has promoted Liam Driscoll to the role of creative executive, Variety has learned exclusively. 

	Driscoll began his time at Be
body:
Berlanti Productions has promoted Liam Driscoll to the role of creative executive, Variety has learned exclusively. 

	Driscoll began his time at Berlanti Productions as Greg Berlanti’s assistant but will now be working across both film and TV. He also previously worked in the mailroom at Anonymous Content. 

	“Liam’s hard work, intelligence, and sharp instincts have been invaluable to us and the company,” said Berlanti and Sarah Schechter. “He has great taste, hustle and his passion and deep respect for storytellers and their visions will be instrumental in bringing new projects to both the film and tv departments and we are so excited to watch him succeed in his new position as Creative Executive at what will be the start of an incredibly successful career.” 
	

	In his new role, Driscoll will be tasked with bringing both film and TV projects into Berlanti Productions and Berlanti Schechter Films, having recently worked with Berlanti as he set up the company’s slate across a variety of platforms. 


	“This is such an exciting time to be at the company,” Driscoll said. “There could be no better education in this business than working for Greg and Sarah. Their integrity and fierce advocacy for creatives is something I learn from each day. It’s a dream to work across projects that champion new exciting voices, while at the same time helping build the kind of classic shows and films that made me fall in love with this industry in the first place.” 

	Berlanti Productions is currently under an overall TV deal at Warner Bros. Television, where the company has been based for the past 15 years. Their current slates includes upcoming shows like “Afterlife with Archie” at Disney+, “Scooby-Doo: Origins” at Netflix, “How to Survive Without Me” at HBO Max, and “Stillwater” at Amazon Prime Video.

            A 6-month-old baby girl was found dead in a dumpster in South Los Angeles ... and her mother is in custody as police investigate the infant's death as a homicide.
      
    
            The baby was discovered in the trash receptacle late Monday night in South L.A. ... though LAPD says the child had been left there sometime in the previous 24 hours.
      
    
            Cops say firefighters responded to the scene and took the baby to a nearby hospital ... where she was pronounced dead.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The LAPD tells TMZ ... officers received a call about a death investigation late Monday for an infant female found in a trash can.
      
    
            LAPD's Juvenile Division is investigating the child's death as a homicide. Officers have already determined the child was not homeless, and the crime is not gang-related.
      
    
            ABC7 reports they had a journalist on the scene who saw the baby's mother placed in handcuffs and taken away in a police vehicle.
      
    
            The outlet also reports they spoke to a couple who said the baby might be their granddaughter. They claimed the daughter gave their grandkid to the child's father around 6 PM Monday, and the family hadn't heard from him.
      
    
            Story developing ...

            A motorist in Texas just couldn't hold it anymore, apparently ... allegedly using his car as a battering ram because nature called and the bathroom was locked.
      
    
            The Rosenberg Police Department -- which operates in a suburb southwest of Houston -- detailed the shocking incident ... claiming a 60-year-old man intentionally drove his car through the pharmacy-side entrance of a Kroger.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Cops say he "intentionally accelerated" through the entrance ... because he allegedly "needed to use the restroom and was upset the doors were locked."
      

            Pics captured the aftermath of the crash ... showing a Chevrolet Equinox parked in the middle of the store, right up against the Halloween candy stand. Shattered glass litters the crash scene, and it looks like the doors are off their hinges.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            According to FOX, officers arrested the driver and charged him with criminal mischief.
      
    
            When ya gotta go, ya gotta go ... though it's unclear if the driver even made it to the toilet.

Presley Gerber

body:
Presley Gerber
                          Last Girlfriend's Emotional Goodbye
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 29, 2026
                            8:09 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Presley Gerber's last girlfriend is remembering their final months together ... sharing selfies and love notes in a touching tribute after his death.
      
    
            Charlie Manley posted a carousel Monday night with several selfies of the couple, a handwritten note from Presley, a bouquet of flowers, and a video of waves crashing.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Charlie called Presley "the most incredible and inspirational human" she'd ever known and said she feels "endlessly lucky" to have loved him -- and been loved by him -- during his final months.
      

            She says ... "What we shared is something I will carry with me for the rest of my life. A true angel. Your beautiful heart and soul will live on with me, forever and always."
      
    
            As we reported ... Presley died Sept. 20 after checking into a Santa Monica sober living facility. His official cause of death remains under investigation, but we're told authorities believe he died of an overdose.
      
    
            We're also told Presley's family has been considering a private memorial at the Gerber family's Malibu home, where loved ones could gather privately to remember him.

title: 'Saved by the Bell' Star Dennis Haskins Dead at 75
description:
'Saved by the Bell' Dennis Haskins
                          Dead at 75
body:
'Saved by the Bell' Dennis Haskins
                          Dead at 75
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 28, 2026
                            7:23 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 29, 2026
                                8:57 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Dennis Haskins, best known for playing Principal Richard Belding on "Saved by the Bell," has died ... TMZ has confirmed.
      
    
            His agent Jay Schachter tells TMZ ... "It's a tragic loss. Everyone loved Mr. Belding and those of us who got to know Dennis, loved him even more. He was a great person, and he loved, I mean absolutely LOVED his fans."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            His cause of death is currently not yet known.
      
    
            He continued ... "He always had time for them, no matter what. He was my client and dear friend for over 20 years, and I will miss him terribly."
      
    
            He became a familiar face to TV viewers in the late 1980s and 1990s as Principal Belding on the hit teen sitcom "Saved by the Bell."
      
    
            His character was constantly trying to keep Zack Morris and the rest of the Bayside High students in line, often delivering his signature catchphrase, "Hey, hey, hey, what is going on here?"
      
    
            Haskins reprised the role in several "Saved by the Bell" spinoffs, including "Saved by the Bell: The College Years" and "Saved by the Bell: The New Class."
      
    
            Dennis was 75.
      
    
            RIP.
